subject: Response: Mosaic Health RFP — IP, Indemnity & Order Form clarifications
messages:
From: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@mosaichealth.org>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mosaic Health Procurement <procurement@mosaichealth.org>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mosaic RFP — Section 4 (IP / Liability) clarifications needed

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the RFP submission. Procurement and legal have a few follow-ups on Section 4 (intellectual property, indemnity, and liability caps) before we can move to commercials. Attached is a short PDF with line-referenced questions. High level items we need clarified:

- For bespoke connectors and integration code created for Mosaic, does Redwood assign IP to the customer or grant a perpetual license?
- Is there any carve-out to the liability cap for data breaches or will standard caps apply?
- Does Redwood accept a mutual indemnity for IP infringement tied to a third party claim?
- Suggested order form language for subscription/usage-based calculations — we want to know if your proposed Order Form can be executed as-is or will require redlines.

We need written responses by end of business 2026-09-03 to keep the timeline for vendor selection. Please copy your legal counterpart if required.

Thanks,
Rachel Stone
Sr. Procurement Manager
Mosaic Health
Attachments: Mosaic_RFP_Section4_Questions.pdf
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@mosaichealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mosaic RFP — Section 4 (IP / Liability) clarifications needed

Rachel — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Laura (legal) to provide precise contract language. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a redlined Order Form and a short DPA.

1) IP for bespoke connectors/integration code: Redwood advocates for a customer-facing perpetual, non-exclusive license to any deliverables we produce specifically for Mosaic (connectors, templates, configuration). Redwood retains ownership of the underlying platform, models, and pre-existing libraries. We can provide a license grant in the Order Form that is limited to your internal use and distribution within Mosaic.

2) Liability cap and carve-outs: Our standard liability cap is described in the Order Form; commercially, we typically propose the greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees. We accept carve-outs for gross negligence and will discuss limited carve-outs for breaches tied to Redwood’s negligent handling of customer data.

3) Indemnity: We are generally open to mutual IP indemnity for third-party claims; we prefer a process clause (notice, control of defense, settlement consent) and a liability allocation consistent with our cap.

4) Order Form execution: Attaching a redline of our standard Order Form with suggested language for the IP license and the cap (see attached). Also including a DPA draft for your security team.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm the proposed cap language and any required carve-outs? Marissa, I’ll send a customer-facing summary and the redline so Rachel has a single document to circulate.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Order_Form_Mosaic_Redline.docx, Redwood_DPA_Draft.pdf
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Mosaic RFP — Section 4 (IP / Liability) clarifications needed

Mateo / Marissa — I reviewed the items and redlined a few areas. Key legal positions follow (summarized for the sales thread):

- IP: Redwood will provide a perpetual, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to bespoke deliverables created for Mosaic, limited to internal use. We will not assign underlying platform IP or model weights. If Mosaic requires assignment of custom code, that is possible but would trigger a separate SOW and commercial consideration.

- Indemnity: Mutual IP indemnity is acceptable with the following guardrails: (a) indemnitor controls defense; (b) indemnitee provides prompt notice and reasonable cooperation; (c) settlements that admit fault or impose ongoing obligations require the indemnitee's consent. We will not accept open-ended indemnities tied to customer-modified code.

- Liability cap: Proposed language — "Except for liability arising from (a) gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (b) Redwood's breach of data protection obligations resulting in a confirmed data breach, Redwood's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 1,000,000 and (ii) the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability."

- Data breach carve-out: We will accept a carve-out for Redwood's deliberate or grossly negligent data handling resulting in unauthorized disclosure. For clarity, security incidents caused by customer misconfiguration or customer-supplied code are excluded.

- Order Form: The attached redline implements the license grant and cap above. I recommend the procurement team accept the redline or propose specific, narrow edits.

I attached a clean DPA and a short summary memo to hand to Mosaic's security reviewers.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference

Rachel — thanks for the questions and for the attachment. Per our legal team's review, please find attached: (1) a redlined Order Form implementing the perpetual license for bespoke deliverables (internal use), (2) our DPA draft, and (3) a short one-page FAQ that maps your Section 4 questions to specific clauses.

Quick answers for your packet:
- IP: Perpetual internal license to custom connectors; platform and models retained by Redwood. If assignment is a must, we can discuss a separate SOW.
- Liability cap: Greater of $1M or 12 months' fees; carve-out for gross negligence and confirmed Redwood-caused data breaches.
- Indemnity: Mutual IP indemnity with standard control-of-defense and settlement consent.

Would you like us to produce a single combined PDF (Order Form + DPA + FAQ) for your legal team to mark up? Also curious on timeline — are you planning to start contract redlines week of 9/6?

Regards,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Laura / Mateo — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from legal/security:

- The IP license language looks acceptable. Procurement will request a written confirmation that connector source will be delivered in object form (compiled) unless an assignment is requested with a separate commercial arrangement.
- Regarding the liability carve-out: Mosaic's CISO asked whether Redwood would expand the data breach carve-out to include a specific remediation commitment (e.g., credit and forensic assistance) in addition to monetary recovery. Can you confirm Redwood's standard breach response commitments?
- SOC 2: Mosaic requires a SOC 2 Type II report for the preceding 12 months. Please indicate latest report date and whether an NDA is required to access the full report.

We intend to circulate your redline to our counsel today and will get back to you with line edits. If possible, please provide a single consolidated PDF (Order Form + DPA + FAQ) for easier redlining.

Thanks,
Daniel Kim
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Mosaic Health
